ActivityView.description:
One activity-feed row on the wire — present-when-meaningful: a field its source
doesn't fill is absent, never a placeholder ``None``-as-a-present-field. ``type`` is
one of ``"chunk-changed"`` / ``"event-logged"`` / ``"runner-changed"``; ``key`` is the
identity of the underlying fact, never a stable frame id.
ActivityView.title: ActivityView

AnswerRequest.description: The body of ``POST /questions/{id}/answer`` — the human's answer.
AnswerRequest.title: AnswerRequest

AnswerResult.description:
The answer write's outcome — first-write-wins CAS.

``won`` is True for the write that landed the row; the loser gets ``won=False`` with
the **winning** row so it can be told who already answered (the 409 body).
AnswerResult.title: AnswerResult

ApplyResponse.description:
The response to a completion submission. Exactly one of ``next_envelope`` (when ``outcome ==
next``) or ``detail`` (on a non-advancing outcome) is meaningful; ``outcome`` discriminates.
ApplyResponse.title: ApplyResponse

ArtifactView.description:
One entry of a chunk's inline artifact store. ``key`` is ``{node}.{artifact-name}.{epoch}`` —
append-only, so latest-by-epoch resolution is the reader's. ``content`` carries an **asset**'s text
verbatim; ``repo``/``branch_name``/``commit_hash`` carry a ``git_commit``'s pinned reference, never
the code. ``branch_url`` is the branch's forge URL. ``recorded_at`` decodes the id's ULID stamp.
ArtifactView.title: ArtifactView

BounceView.description:
One recorded delivery kick-back (#64) — contention, not failure, and never itself a status.
``envelope`` is the raw JSON kick-back payload verbatim.
BounceView.title: BounceView

CheckResult.description:
One deterministic check's **runner-executed** outcome (issue #114).

Carries only ``(command, passed)``; the runner's captured ``output_tail``
deliberately does not ride the wire.
CheckResult.title: CheckResult

ChunkDetail.description:
The chunk aggregate in full, carrying its **transition history** — every node it visited,
including a review that failed and looped back — and its inline **artifact store**.
ChunkDetail.title: ChunkDetail

ChunkGroupRequest.description:
Merge unacquired chunks into one.

``merge_chunk_ids`` fold into the path's survivor, which absorbs the union of their
work refs. Self-references and duplicates are ignored; a non-ready member is ``409``.
ChunkGroupRequest.title: ChunkGroupRequest

ChunkGroupResponse.description: The survivor chunk after a group — its id and the union of work refs it carries.
ChunkGroupResponse.title: ChunkGroupResponse

ChunkIngestRequest.description:
Ingest by source-native token — specific items always, batch fine. Each token is resolved against
the configured work sources' own grammar: ``{name}:{ref}``, ``{name}#{ref}``, or the item's own URL.
Tokens only; no pre-resolved ``{source, ref}`` shape travels alongside them (pinned by
tests/test_pin_wire.py::test_chunk_ingest_accepts_source_native_tokens_only).
ChunkIngestRequest.title: ChunkIngestRequest

ChunkPatchRequest.description:
The multi-field ``PATCH /chunks/{id}`` body (issue #124) — every field independently optional,
applied all-or-nothing. ``graph_id``/``model`` mean "leave unchanged" whether omitted or explicitly
``null``. ``intended_migration`` *is* nullable, so omitted ("leave unchanged") stays distinguishable
from explicit ``null`` ("clear it") via ``model_fields_set``, never this field's own value.
ChunkPatchRequest.title: ChunkPatchRequest

ChunkPatchResponse.description:
The result of one ``PATCH /chunks/{id}`` (issues #124, #144) — the chunk's editable build
properties after the edit, carried together since a PATCH can apply more than one at once.
ChunkPatchResponse.title: ChunkPatchResponse

ChunkPauseRequest.description: Set or clear a chunk's operator pause brake — records who flipped it (issue #46).
ChunkPauseRequest.title: ChunkPauseRequest

ChunkStatus.description: The derived chunk statuses. Never stored — always a query result.
ChunkStatus.title: ChunkStatus

ChunkStopRequest.description: Terminally abandon a chunk — records who stopped it (issue #118).
ChunkStopRequest.title: ChunkStopRequest

ChunkSummary.description:
One row of the fleet chunk list — the derived status and current node. ``current_node_name`` is
the node's human graph name beside the raw ``nd_`` ULID, null when unresolvable.
``runner_id``/``environment_count`` are **in-progress-only** (issue #140): a terminal chunk reads
unrouted even while its route facts stand. ``completed_at`` is the terminal instant, else null.
ChunkSummary.title: ChunkSummary

ChunkUsageTotalView.description:
A chunk's derived usage/cost total, summed over every recorded invocation (issue #59) — never a
stored column. ``cost_partial`` carries the lower-bound + PARTIAL contract on ``cost_usd``; see
:class:`~blizzard.hub.domain.work.UsageTotal` for the one canonical statement of it.
ChunkUsageTotalView.title: ChunkUsageTotalView

ChunkUsageView.description:
One node-step's usage/cost telemetry (issue #59) — one harness invocation's tokens-by-class and
cost, oldest first on :class:`ChunkDetail`. ``cost_usd`` is ``None`` exactly when no result envelope
existed for this invocation — never fabricated.
ChunkUsageView.title: ChunkUsageView

CliTokenRequest.description: ``POST /api/auth/cli/token``'s body (issue #96) — the CLI's PKCE code exchange.
CliTokenRequest.title: CliTokenRequest

CliTokenResponse.description: The minted hub session token (decision D6) — never a runner-style JWT.
CliTokenResponse.title: CliTokenResponse

CompletionSubmission.description: A node-step's completion — judgement choice + checks + artifacts + epoch.
CompletionSubmission.title: CompletionSubmission

DecisionResolutionRequest.description: A person's choice for an open decision — first-write-wins CAS.
DecisionResolutionRequest.title: DecisionResolutionRequest

DecisionResolutionResponse.description: The winning resolution — the choice, who, and when.
DecisionResolutionResponse.title: DecisionResolutionResponse

DecisionSubmission.description:
A runner-config gate: submit a decision in place of a transition.

Carries the gated step's artifacts and its fencing epoch as one atomic write; the
node's choice set is resolved from the pinned graph, not sent here.
DecisionSubmission.title: DecisionSubmission

DecisionView.description:
A gate decision in full.

``resolved_choice`` is set once a person has decided; ``transitioned`` is true once the
resolving transition has been recorded.
DecisionView.title: DecisionView

EnvelopeArtifact.description: One artifact carried into a node-step, resolved latest-by-epoch.
EnvelopeArtifact.title: EnvelopeArtifact

EnvelopeChoice.description: A selectable outcome the worker's judgement may emit.
EnvelopeChoice.title: EnvelopeChoice

EscalationReport.title: EscalationReport

EscalationView.description:
An open escalation on a ``needs_human`` chunk — the takeover command(s) for the parked session,
present only while the escalation is open; a later lease mint supersedes it.
``wrapped_takeover_command`` is optional, empty when none was composed.
EscalationView.title: EscalationView

EventView.description:
One operational event on the wire — an ``event_log`` row or a projected open
escalation. ``chunk_id``/``lease_id``/``node_name`` are absent for a runner-scoped
event; ``runner_id`` is absent for a projected escalation (issue #155 — ``null``,
never ``""``); ``detail`` is the event-specific JSON payload.
EventView.title: EventView

EventsResponse.description: The operational event feed, newest-and-most-severe first (bounded).
EventsResponse.title: EventsResponse

ExternalSubscriptionUsageView.description: A runner's newest sampled external-subscription-usage snapshot (issue #218).
ExternalSubscriptionUsageView.title: ExternalSubscriptionUsageView

ExternalSubscriptionUsageWindowView.description:
One rate-limit window's utilization, as the harness's own account reported it
(issue #218) — ``window`` is the harness-native label, ``utilization_pct`` is 0-100,
``resets_at`` the reset instant, ``window_seconds`` the window's length.
ExternalSubscriptionUsageWindowView.title: ExternalSubscriptionUsageWindowView

FleetSpendView.description:
The fleet's usage/cost total since ``since`` and, when the caller bounded the
window, strictly before ``until`` (``None`` for the open-ended tail). ``cost_partial``
marks ``cost_usd`` as a lower bound — see :class:`~blizzard.hub.domain.work.UsageTotal`.
FleetSpendView.title: FleetSpendView

FleetSummaryView.title: FleetSummaryView

GraphChoiceView.description: One selectable outcome of a node's judgement.
GraphChoiceView.title: GraphChoiceView

GraphEdgeView.description: A directed, choice-keyed connection between two nodes of one graph.
GraphEdgeView.title: GraphEdgeView

GraphLifecycleRequest.description: Retire or re-enable a graph — records who flipped it (issue #101).
GraphLifecycleRequest.title: GraphLifecycleRequest

GraphMintRequest.description: A graph definition to mint — the raw YAML body.
GraphMintRequest.title: GraphMintRequest

GraphNodeView.description: A reified node in a minted graph — the full immutable definition.
GraphNodeView.title: GraphNodeView

GraphPolicyRequest.description:
Set a graph's follow-latest policy — the tri-state (issue #164).

``follow_latest`` is required and carries no default: ``true``/``false`` override the
hub-level setting for this mint's chunks, explicit ``null`` reverts to inheriting it.
GraphPolicyRequest.title: GraphPolicyRequest

GraphSessionView.description:
One graph-level named session declaration (issue #144).

``model`` is a prioritized preference list of opaque strings, resolved left-to-right at
session mint; the hub interprets neither it nor ``effort``.
GraphSessionView.title: GraphSessionView

GraphSummaryView.description:
One graph's summary row — a name-lineage entry as served by ``GET /graphs``.

``effective`` marks the newest **non-retired** graph of this ``name`` (issue #101), while
``retired`` is this graph's own state: a non-retired non-effective graph is superseded.
GraphSummaryView.title: GraphSummaryView

GraphSyncEntry.description:
One packaged graph's reconciliation outcome (issue #146).

``status`` is ``minted``, ``up-to-date``, or ``failed``; ``graph_id`` is present only on
``minted``, and ``detail`` says why a graph minted or what went wrong.
GraphSyncEntry.title: GraphSyncEntry

GraphSyncResponse.description:
``POST /graphs/sync``'s report — one entry per packaged graph (issue #146).

``ok`` is false iff any entry failed, so a caller gates on the field rather than
re-deriving it. Always ``200``: a per-graph failure is data, not a transport error.
GraphSyncResponse.title: GraphSyncResponse

GraphView.description:
A minted graph as served by ``GET /graphs/{graph_id}`` and the mint response.

``enabled`` and ``retired`` are one lifecycle fact (issue #101), saying nothing about
whether this mint is newest. ``follow_latest`` is the **stored** tri-state (#164).
GraphView.title: GraphView

HubAdvanceResponse.description:
The result of one on-demand hub-advance (#65). A generic hub command node runs ``run:`` to
completion, one call at a time, behind the fleet-wide serialization slot: ``ran=False`` means the
slot was held by a different chunk and this call deferred without touching anything — not an
error.
HubAdvanceResponse.title: HubAdvanceResponse

HubMarkerResponse.description: The recorded marker — ``recorded=False`` iff it already existed (idempotent).
HubMarkerResponse.title: HubMarkerResponse

IntendedMigrationPatch.description:
The intended-migration value a :class:`ChunkPatchRequest` carries (issue #124). ``to_graph`` is a
graph id, or a name resolved server-side to the newest enabled graph of that name at request time —
the resolved **id** is stored. ``node`` present selects ``forced``, absent selects ``auto``; there
is no separate ``mode`` field, so "node supplied under auto" is unrepresentable.
IntendedMigrationPatch.title: IntendedMigrationPatch

IntendedMigrationView.description:
A chunk's standing migration intent (issue #124) — editable at any non-terminal status and
consulted, never applied eagerly, at the chunk's next transition. ``graph_name`` is resolved
server-side from the stored ``graph_id``, null when unresolvable. ``node_name`` is the ``forced``
mode's landing target, null for ``auto``, whose landing is derived at consult time.
IntendedMigrationView.title: IntendedMigrationView

JudgedBy.description: Who renders a node's exit judgement — the structural gate marker.
JudgedBy.title: JudgedBy

LeaseMintReport.description: A runner's ``lease.minted`` — one node-step attempt's fencing epoch.
LeaseMintReport.title: LeaseMintReport

MeResponse.description: The resolved identity's wire view — the board's own-identity read.
MeResponse.title: MeResponse

MigrationMode.description:
How a chunk's :class:`IntendedMigration` fires at its next transition (issue #124).

``AUTO`` fires only when the transition's own destination node name also exists on
the target graph; ``FORCED`` fires unconditionally onto the intent's ``node_name``.
MigrationMode.title: MigrationMode

MigrationView.description:
One cross-graph migration step (issue #90): the chunk's attempt ended in ``from_graph`` and it
re-queued at ``landed_node`` in ``to_graph`` — its own step, never a transition
(``bzh:migration-not-transition``). ``model`` is the re-pinned model, null when the chunk kept its
own. ``source`` says what moved it: ``authored-edge``, ``intent``, or ``follow-latest`` (#164).
MigrationView.title: MigrationView

NodeConfig.description: The node's invariant identity for this step.
NodeConfig.title: NodeConfig

NodeEnvelope.description: Everything a runner needs to work one node-step.
NodeEnvelope.title: NodeEnvelope

OpenDecisionsResponse.description: The fleet's open (unresolved) decisions — ``blizzard hub decisions``.
OpenDecisionsResponse.title: OpenDecisionsResponse

PauseView.description:
An open pause on a chunk (issue #46) — who set it and when, present only while ``paused=True``
is the newest pause fact. Carried independently of ``status``: PAUSED sits below the human-gated
statuses in the derivation order, so this is the only carrier of a pause on a gated chunk.
PauseView.title: PauseView

PendingView.description:
A hub node's in-progress poll (#66) — whether a chunk parked at a hub node is about to run its
first attempt or is already mid-poll, and when the next is due. Never itself a status.
PendingView.title: PendingView

PrView.description: An open PR a chunk is parked on in open-pr delivery mode.
PrView.title: PrView

ProducesEntry.description:
One node's ``produces:`` expectation, kind-carrying (D1, issue #143).

The wire counterpart of :class:`~blizzard.hub.domain.graph.ProducesSpec`, so every
surface carrying a ``produces:`` entry carries the same kind-carrying shape.
ProducesEntry.title: ProducesEntry

ProviderSummary.description: One configured provider, as ``GET /api/auth/providers`` lists it.
ProviderSummary.title: ProviderSummary

QuestionAsked.description:
A ``question.asked`` fact the runner forwards to the hub.

``question_id`` is runner-minted (``qn_<ulid>``); ``epoch`` is the parked lease's
fence, ``session_id`` the dormant session, ``options`` the offered choices.
QuestionAsked.title: QuestionAsked

QuestionView.title: QuestionView

QueuePeekEntry.description: One ready chunk, in queue order.
QueuePeekEntry.title: QueuePeekEntry

QueuePeekResponse.description: The ready queue, in the hub's explicit order.
QueuePeekResponse.title: QueuePeekResponse

QueuePositionRequest.description:
Single-chunk fractional reposition — ``POST /api/queue/position`` (issue #137).

``after_chunk_id=null`` moves ``chunk_id`` to the top, otherwise immediately after
the named chunk. Both must be ready (``409``); a self-anchor is ``422``.
QueuePositionRequest.title: QueuePositionRequest

QueueReplaceRequest.description:
Idempotent whole-order replacement of the ready queue — ``PUT /api/queue``.

``chunk_ids`` is the desired order, front to back; each must name a ready chunk
(``409``) and not repeat (``422``). An unnamed ready chunk is appended, order kept.
QueueReplaceRequest.title: QueueReplaceRequest

ReadinessResponse.description: The wire shape of a readiness reading (openapi-ts consumes this).
ReadinessResponse.title: ReadinessResponse

RoleAssignmentRequest.description:
``POST /api/users/{id}/role`` body — the target role, by its ``auth_core.Role``
value.
RoleAssignmentRequest.title: RoleAssignmentRequest

RouteClaim.description: A complete route fact posted by the claiming runner.
RouteClaim.title: RouteClaim

RouteClaimResponse.description:
The winning claim's reply — the route, its first node envelope, and the
route's plaintext capability token (issue #84a), returned exactly once here.
RouteClaimResponse.title: RouteClaimResponse

RouteTokenRekeyResponse.description:
A fresh plaintext route capability token for the chunk's live route (issue #84b),
returned exactly once here.
RouteTokenRekeyResponse.title: RouteTokenRekeyResponse

RouteView.description: A chunk's route — where it is being worked.
RouteView.title: RouteView

RunnerEnrollmentResponse.description:
A freshly minted (or rotated) bearer token — issue #86a.

``token`` is the plaintext, visible only here — only its sha256 hash is kept. A
re-enroll rotates: the old token stops resolving the moment this response lands.
RunnerEnrollmentResponse.title: RunnerEnrollmentResponse

RunnerFact.title: RunnerFact

RunnerFactAck.description:
The hub's per-batch acknowledgement against its high-water mark.

``high_water`` is the new mark after this batch; ``applied``/``already_applied`` partition
the pushed seqs, and ``rejected`` names seqs refused for a non-idempotency reason.
RunnerFactAck.title: RunnerFactAck

RunnerFactBatch.description: A runner's push of one-or-more buffered facts, ordered by seq.
RunnerFactBatch.title: RunnerFactBatch

RunnerListResponse.description: The fleet registry — every registered runner with its liveness.
RunnerListResponse.title: RunnerListResponse

RunnerPauseRequest.description: Set a runner's pause brake — records who flipped it.
RunnerPauseRequest.title: RunnerPauseRequest

RunnerRegistrationRequest.description:
Register a runner into the fleet — runner id + workspace binding.

``env_capacity`` is the runner's configured environment-pool size; ``None`` when the
client reports none, never a guessed total. Re-registration overwrites it.
RunnerRegistrationRequest.title: RunnerRegistrationRequest

RunnerRegistrationResponse.description: The registered runner's id, and whether this call first created its row.
RunnerRegistrationResponse.title: RunnerRegistrationResponse

RunnerView.description:
One fleet-registry row — derived liveness, both brakes, and an advisory snapshot.

The two brakes stay separate (issues #43, #45): ``hub_paused`` is claims-only, while
``locally_paused`` answers "is it spawning at all?". The usage snapshot is advisory.
RunnerView.title: RunnerView

SidechainSegmentView-Input.description:
A subagent's private conversation, nested under its spawning tool call — mirrors
:class:`~blizzard.runner.harness.transcript.SidechainConversation`. Recursive: a
sidechain turn may itself carry a tool call whose own sidechain nests further.
SidechainSegmentView-Input.title: SidechainSegmentView

SidechainSegmentView-Output.description:
A subagent's private conversation, nested under its spawning tool call — mirrors
:class:`~blizzard.runner.harness.transcript.SidechainConversation`. Recursive: a
sidechain turn may itself carry a tool call whose own sidechain nests further.
SidechainSegmentView-Output.title: SidechainSegmentView

SubmittedArtifact.description: An artifact committed atomically with the completion.
SubmittedArtifact.title: SubmittedArtifact

TranscriptSegmentAck.description:
The hub's per-batch acknowledgement against the transcript lane's high-water mark.

``capped`` is D6's cap-rejection class — acknowledged, content-dropped, and the
high-water advances past it, a durable decision that must not re-adjudicate on replay.
TranscriptSegmentAck.title: TranscriptSegmentAck

TranscriptSegmentBatch.description:
A runner's push of one-or-more buffered transcript records, ordered by ``seq`` —
the transcript lane's own store-and-forward batch, distinct from the fact lane's
``RunnerFactBatch`` (D7).
TranscriptSegmentBatch.title: TranscriptSegmentBatch

TranscriptSegmentContentView.description:
One segment's decompressed turns, concatenated across its stored records in
turn-range order — the lazy per-segment content read (D12).
TranscriptSegmentContentView.title: TranscriptSegmentContentView

TranscriptSegmentIndexEntry.description:
One segment's metadata row (D12) — byte counts and completion state, never turn
content. ``truncated`` surfaces D5's per-segment cap-rejection mark now rather than
deferring the board (#248) into a route reshape (plan-review F2).
TranscriptSegmentIndexEntry.title: TranscriptSegmentIndexEntry

TranscriptSegmentIndexView.description:
The per-chunk segment discovery read (D12) — unreachable content, only what a
caller needs to then ask for one segment's turns.
TranscriptSegmentIndexView.title: TranscriptSegmentIndexView

TranscriptSegmentRecord.description:
One shipped turn-range slice of a segment (D1). ``final=True`` marks the one
record that closes the segment out — the hub never infers completeness from a
transition (product plan, ``epic:transcripts``).
TranscriptSegmentRecord.title: TranscriptSegmentRecord

TransitionView.description:
One accepted transition in a chunk's history: the edge a node-step took — origin node, the
judgement choice that routed it, destination — oldest first on the detail.
``from_node_name``/``to_node_name`` are the nodes' human graph names, null when unresolvable.
``graph_id``/``graph_name`` name the graph this step happened in (issue #90), both null on old rows.
TransitionView.title: TransitionView

TurnSegmentView-Input.description:
One normalized turn, carried in full — mirrors :class:`~blizzard.runner.harness.transcript.NormalizedTurn`.
``index``'s stability is per-producer: **segment-relative** and stable (D9) from the shipping lane, but
batch-local and read-unstable, sliding with the recency window, from the runner's lease-transcript route
(blizzard#248 D1). ``kind`` is closed — ``docs/versioning.md``.
TurnSegmentView-Input.title: TurnSegmentView

TurnSegmentView-Output.description:
One normalized turn, carried in full — mirrors :class:`~blizzard.runner.harness.transcript.NormalizedTurn`.
``index``'s stability is per-producer: **segment-relative** and stable (D9) from the shipping lane, but
batch-local and read-unstable, sliding with the recency window, from the runner's lease-transcript route
(blizzard#248 D1). ``kind`` is closed — ``docs/versioning.md``.
TurnSegmentView-Output.title: TurnSegmentView

UserView.description: One ``users`` row — the listing/assignment response shape.
UserView.title: UserView

WorkItemEntry.description:
One pointer's pass-through work item — title, body, and comment thread, vendor-native.
``label``/``web_url`` are the legible pointer label and its browser address, both null when no
configured source names ``source``. A per-pointer failure degrades here rather than failing the
whole read: ``error`` carries the reason and ``title``/``body`` are null.
WorkItemEntry.title: WorkItemEntry

WorkItemsView.description:
A chunk's pass-through work items — one entry per pointer, order preserved.

Empty when the chunk holds no pointers; a grouped chunk carrying many pointers
yields one entry per pointer, each fetched fresh and never stored.
WorkItemsView.title: WorkItemsView

WorkRefModel.description:
One ``{source, ref}`` work ref — ``source`` names a configured
``[[work_source]]``; ``ref`` is that source's own item token.
WorkRefModel.title: WorkRefModel

WorkRefView.title: WorkRefView

blizzard__wire__envelope__RotatePolicyVi.description:
The declared session's rotation bounds (issue #144), carried on :class:`NodeConfig`.
``max_invocations`` counts **harness invocations** — spawn, resume, judge, nudge — not node-steps,
of which one burns two or three.
blizzard__wire__envelope__RotatePolicyVi.title: RotatePolicyView

blizzard__wire__graph__RotatePolicyView.description:
One declared session's rotation bounds (issue #144).

Every threshold is independently optional; ``max_invocations`` counts **harness
invocations**, not node-steps, one of which burns several.
blizzard__wire__graph__RotatePolicyView.title: RotatePolicyView

get.description:
The activity backfill (issue #213) — the three already-bounded per-source activity reads merged,
sorted newest-first, and capped.

``since`` defaults to 24h before the injected clock's own ``now()``, never ``datetime.now()``. A
tz-naive ``since`` is coerced to UTC so it never raises against the store's aware timestamps.

post.description:
Redeem a ``client=cli`` authorize code for a hub session token (issue #96).

Public plane — there is no session yet; this route is what mints one. One
undifferentiated 400 covers every failure, telling a caller nothing about which.

schema.title: Response Jwks Api Auth Jwks Json Get
Response List Providers Api Auth Providers Get

post.description:
Mint a fresh current signing key, demoting the old current to previous (issue
#95). Human-plane, gated on ``user:manage`` and closed to a runner bearer token.

get.description: The fleet chunk list — derived status per chunk.

schema.title: Response List Chunks Api Chunks Get

post.description:
Ingest by source-native token; 422 on a token no configured source
claims; 409 on a pointer held by a live chunk; 503 if every graph named after the
packaged default has been retired (issue #101 — the operator's brake, not a code
bug: re-enable one or mint a new one).

get.description: One chunk aggregate in full — derived status, current node, route.

patch.description:
Apply the body's fields in one all-or-nothing edit (issue #124).

404 only when the chunk is unknown; :class:`ChunkPatchBody` and ``EditService.edit``
own every other refusal.

post.description: Forcibly release a chunk from its runner without touching any escalation.

Merge unacquired chunks into ``chunk_id``.

Accepts ``not_ready`` and ``ready`` participants alike (issue #141); 409 names the
first chunk a runner holds, or one already finished.

The mid-run marker callback (#65) — a ``run:`` step's own dynamic-loop marker.

Records a marker artifact mid-run, ahead of the producing command's own exit.
Idempotent per ``(chunk, node, name, epoch)``.
Set a chunk's operator pause brake — the claim is kept, unlike detach (issue #46).

get.description: Deprecated since issue #55 — use `GET /chunks/{chunk_id}/work-items`, which this path aliases onto the identical handler and returns the identical view.

post.description:
Promote a not-ready chunk to ready so a runner may claim it.

Idempotent: promoting an already-ready or already-running chunk is a harmless no-op.
404 only when the chunk is unknown.
Close an escalation by supersession: requeue at the current node.
Clear a chunk's operator pause brake — idempotent, never refused (issue #46).

Terminally abandon CHUNK — the operator's last-resort verb (issue #118).

Records the ``chunk_stopped`` fact so the chunk derives ``stopped`` and never
re-derives ``ready``, and releases any live route in the same operation. 409 when
the chunk is already ``done`` or ``stopped`` — stopping is not retroactive.

get.description: The chunk's segment index (D12) — metadata and byte counts only, never turns.

One segment's decompressed turns, concatenated across its stored records in
turn-range order — the lazy per-segment content read (D12).

Pass-through work items read — one entry per pointer, contents never stored.

A per-pointer resolution or forge failure degrades to an ``error`` on that entry
rather than failing the whole read. A chunk with no pointers is an empty list, not
a 404; no configured work source at all is a 503 up front.
The fleet's open (unresolved) decisions — gate surfacing.

post.description:
Resolve an open decision, first-write-wins CAS.

``resolved_by`` is taken from the resolved session identity
(:func:`~blizzard.hub.api.auth_session.resolved_username`), never the request
body's ``resolved_by`` field — a spoofed value there is silently ignored (issue #91).

get.description:
The ``event_log`` unified with open escalations (issue #125), most-severe-newest first, bounded.

The ``severity`` / ``runner_id`` / ``chunk_id`` / ``since`` filters apply to the ``event_log`` half;
the open-escalation projection is always unioned in. A tz-naive ``since`` is coerced to UTC so the
projection's aware ``recorded_at`` comparison below never raises against it.
The runner's chunk-status poll — the same aggregate as the board's own read.

post.description: Apply a node-step's completion atomically; reply carries the next envelope.
Runner-config gate: park the chunk on a decision in place of a transition.

get.description: The chunk's current node envelope, idempotent — the lost-apply re-read.

post.description: Land a runner's ``escalation.recorded`` — the chunk derives ``needs_human``.

schema.title: Response Report Escalation Api Fleet Chunks  Chunk Id  Escalations Post

post.description:
Drive a chunk parked at a generic hub command node one step (#65), running
:class:`~blizzard.hub.delivery.hub_node.HubNodeExecutor` once under the fleet-wide serialization
slot. ``ran=False`` is never an error: a different chunk holds the slot, or (#66) the node reported
